notes.title: '83 Technical Test - September 19-21
notes.content:
'83 Technical Test
We're excited to announce that this weekend, September 19th-21st we will be running a limited scope Technical Test as a part of our overall preparations for our Early Access launch later this year.

If you want to participate, head over to the '83 Steam Store page right now and click the "Request Access" button.

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1059220/83/"][/dynamiclink]Steam will notify you if you were accepted within a maximum of couple of hours, and if we need further testers during the weekend we may allow in additional waves.

Please note that this Technical Test is under strict NDA and no sharing of screenshots or videos is permitted and we reserve the right to revoke your Technical Test access if footage/screenshots is leaked.


Technical Test Schedule
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34826071/a86033083b345ca41ef8054360a4a5ab531cd474.jpg"]
FAQ


This is my first Technical Test, what should I expect as a player? 

The build you will play is truly a work-in-progress and you can expect to see some unfinished assets, missing textures and of course encounter bugs. We want to involve our community as early as possible in the development process and to do that we will be offering access to builds that are less polished than what you might be used to from other tests or Beta’s you’ve participated in. 



Why are the servers limited to 30v30, while the Steam page advertises 40v40? 

It's important for us to ensure a smooth testing experience for all our players during this technical test. To ensure this, we temporarily lowered the playercount to a max of 60 as there still is ongoing optimisation work to support 80 players while also ensuring quality server performance. 

This is a temporary measure for testing purposes only, the Early Access release is still planned to support 80 player, 40v40 servers. 



I launched the game but can’t find any active servers? 

The technical is not 24/7 and takes place during specific timeslots, please see the infographics above for the exact timings. 



Outside of these hours, you can still launch the game and check settings, keybinds etc. but you won’t be able to connect to a server and play. 



I requested access but haven’t been accepted or received any further information, why is this? 

This is a limited scope technical test, and once we hit the required number of players we will stop accepting new players. There is a possibility that we might let additional players in if we need additional testers during the test – so make sure to request access through Steam even if we’re currently full! 



I am a current Alpha playtester, do I need to request access? 

If you are one of our current Alpha playtesters with access to the game, you do not need to request access – all our current playtesters will have automatic access to this technical test. 



What should I be doing as a playtester, are there any specific tasks or focus for participating players? 

There are no specific testing needs to be done, we encourage you to play the game as you normally would and provide us with your honest feedback and submit bug reports on these dedicated pages: 

Bugs & Feedback Link: https://83thegame.com/feedback/

 

I am a content creator/streamer and would like to create content around the test, is this allowed? 

No, this current test is under NDA and we don’t allow the capture of the gameplay for use in content creation purposes. If needed due to leaks, we might have to submit a copyright infringement claim on I.E. YouTube/Twitch to take it down – and we don’t want that any more than you do. 

Intentional leaking will result in your access to the Technical Test being revoked. 

You as a creator will have plenty of opportunities to create content around ‘83 in the future, and we are also keen on working closely together with creators as we move closer to our Early Access launch later this year. 



I encountered a bug, or have feedback on the game at large – where do I share/report it? 

Submit all your bug reports and feedback on our official website, due to the NDA this is the only place you can submit these. Do not share them on other channels, including our official Discord for now. 

Bugs & Feedback Link: https://83thegame.com/feedback/

 

Looking forward to your honest feedback and bug reports! 



Am I allowed to capture/screenshot the game as a part of my bug report and feedback submissions? 

Yes, you are allowed to capture video and screenshot the game as long as that footage only gets submitted through our official website forms for bug reporting and feedback collection. 



Does this Technical Test represent the scope of content that will be available for Early Access release? 

No, while both Early Access launch factions are in, the U.S. Army and Soviet Ground Forces – only one map is available in the Technical Test and the playable tanks are also not available during this test. 

Further content updates are also planned following our Early Access release. 



I found a player who is breaking community standards and/or leaking the content, where do I report this? 

You can report players through our official website form and we will take the appropriate action from there. 

Please provide proof through screenshots or other relevant pieces of information. 

Examples of breaking community standards: 

Intentional Teamkilling. 

Intentional Trolling. 

Inappropriate In-Game Behavior. (Racist, Sexist, Homophobic etc.) 

Leaking Technical Test content. (Screenshots and screen captures/videos etc.) 

Report Link: https://83thegame.com/feedback/

notes.title: '83 - Developer Tapes #3 - Classes
notes.content:
Dev Diary #3 – Classes
Welcome back to our series of Developer Tapes leading up to our early access launch. 

Today we take a closer look at the classes within '83 and how each class have their own role to play on the battlefield.


[previewyoutube="ZPYT_BC4toM;full"][/previewyoutube]
In ‘83, victory depends on coordination, role discipline, and the decisions you make before you even fire a shot.



Every match begins with a crucial choice: your class. This determines your weapons, equipment, and overall role on the battlefield. Each class is grounded in authentic Cold War doctrine, with loadouts shaped by the arsenals of the 1983 U.S. Army and Soviet Ground Forces. 



While both factions share most core roles, you’ll notice subtle differences in the tools and equipment available, reflecting the real-world divergences between East and West at the time. 



Classes offer limited loadout customisation through a slot-based system. Want to move fast and light? Ditch extra gear. Need more utility? Carry smoke, frags, or anti-tank weapons. But every added item has a weight cost, affecting stamina and movement, meaning each loadout choice comes with trade-offs. 



Infantry squads consist of 10 players: one Squad Leader and nine soldiers. Squads share a dedicated VOIP channel, allowing for coordinated movement, objective marking, and the placement of temporary squad-only spawn points. These spawn points are powerful tools, but they’re fragile, can be disabled by nearby enemies, and come with a longer respawn timer. Protect them and use them wisely. 



Each class in ‘83 plays a distinct part: 

Rifleman – The backbone of the platoon, armed with standard issue rifles and grenades. 

Machine Gunner – Provides suppressive fire and anchors defensive positions. 

Marksman – Picks off high-value targets at range, avoiding direct engagements. 

Grenadier – Clears entrenched enemies and denies ground using their underbarrel grenade launcher. 

Anti-Tank – Specialised in disabling and destroying enemy vehicles. 

Tank Crew – Minimally armed, but the only class capable of operating armoured vehicles. 

Special Forces and NCOs – Specialist roles with unique tactical capabilities we’ll be showcasing in more detail as development progresses through Early Access. 

Class availability is limited to preserve balance. If all sniper slots are filled, you’ll need to choose another class, or wait. Squads also have internal class limits, encouraging a functional, complementary mix of roles to keep gameplay tactical and dynamic. 



Squad Leaders aren’t just fielding orders, they’re tactical lynchpins. With access to specialised gear and a direct command channel linking them to other squad leaders and the team’s Commander, their decisions shape the pace and positioning of the team. Squad Leaders can name, lock, manage, and restructure their squads on the fly, while also placing rally points and setting the tone for engagements. 



At the top sits the Commander, one per team, who plays the game from a strategic perspective, managing the battle via an RTS-style command interface. They issue orders, coordinate squads, manage resources, and deploy powerful abilities, from artillery and smoke barrages to recon flights and rapid reinforcements. Commanders are valuable, and vulnerable.  



From the front-line Rifleman to the Commander orchestrating strikes from above, ‘83 is built to reward co-ordination, teamwork, and knowing your role. Whether you're holding the line, clearing bunkers, or pushing behind enemy positions, your decisions shape the outcome of every battle.

notes.title: '83 - Developer Tapes #2 - Factions
notes.content:
Dev Diary #2 – Factions 
Welcome back to our series of ‘83 Dev Diary series leading up to our early access launch. 

In this instalment, we’re turning our focus to the two military powers at the heart of the conflict: the United States Army and the Soviet Ground Forces. 


[previewyoutube="vHdqd1bVKg0;full"][/previewyoutube]


A major inspiration for the game’s setting comes from a real historical event - Able Archer 83. In November of that year, NATO ran a large-scale exercise simulating an escalation to nuclear war. Though intended as a drill, it was interpreted by the Soviet Union as a potential first strike. Soviet forces went on high alert. For several tense days, the world sat on the edge of full-scale war. 

It’s this high-stakes tension, the sense that one misstep could change everything that forms the foundation of ‘83. In our version of history, diplomacy breaks down and the Cold War turns hot. 

To build this world authentically, the team has spent years researching the era, drawing from military archives, photo references, re-enactment groups, Cold War museums, and consultations with military history communities. The result is a grounded depiction of the factions, their equipment, and their doctrine, accurate to what would have been in widespread use in 1983. 


United States Army
In ‘83, the US Army is built around structure, fire discipline, and precision. Players will have access to a wide array of authentic weapons from the era, including the M16A1, the M60 LMG and the M21 SWS. 

Each class within the US faction has a defined role. US Special Forces introduce further specialisation with close-quarters tools like combat shotguns. Gear is consistent and modernise, standardised uniforms, with machined parts and synthetic materials that reflect the transition from post-WWII military kits to a more agile force. 


Soviet Ground Forces
Opposing them, the Soviet Ground Forces embody a doctrine of pressure, volume, and momentum. In ’83 you can choose from a variety of iconic weapons like the AK-74, the PKM and the RPG-7, which allow Soviet squads to apply constant forward pressure across the battlefield. Their tactics revolve around massed infantry pushes, massed firepower, and armored vehicle support. 

Soviet equipment also tells a different story. Uniforms are more rugged and made from natural materials such as canvas, leather, and repurposed stock. This reflects the utilitarian, production-focused mindset of the Eastern Bloc, where practicality often outweighed aesthetics. 

[img src="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAAAXNSR0IArs4c6QAAAARnQU1BAACxjwv8YQUAAAAJcEhZcwAADsMAAA7DAcdvqGQAAAANSURBVBhXY2BgYGAAAAAFAAGKM+MAAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"] 
A Clash of Doctrines
In ‘83, each faction allows you to bring each faction’s philosophy, equipment, and battlefield doctrine to the fight. Play as the US and choose to adopt the strategies of fire discipline, coordination, and role-based tactics. Or play as he Soviets and pile on the pressure, with numbers, and volume of fire. Two distinct potential approaches. One contested battlefield. Victory will go to the team that best understands and plays to their strengths and group tactics. 

[img src="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAAAXNSR0IArs4c6QAAAARnQU1BAACxjwv8YQUAAAAJcEhZcwAADsMAAA7DAcdvqGQAAAANSURBVBhXY2BgYGAAAAAFAAGKM+MAAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"] 
Coming Up Next
In our next dev diary, we’ll be breaking down the many playable roles in ’83, from frontline riflemen and anti-tank specialists to the Commander, who oversees the flow of the battle with powerful off-map support. Each role plays a critical part in shaping the outcome of every fight, and we’re excited to show you how squad tactics and strategic planning come together to create intense, large-scale Cold War combat. 

Stay tuned, and thanks for your continued support.

notes.title: '83 - Developer Tapes #1 - Overview of the Game
notes.content:
Dev Diary #1 – Welcome to ‘83 
Welcome to the first in our new dev diary series for ‘83! Whether you’ve been following the project for a while or are just hearing about it now, this is where we’ll be sharing updates straight from the team as we build our toward Early Access release.


What is ‘83? 
‘83 is a Cold War FPS where NATO and the Warsaw Pact where tensions quickly escalate into a full-blown war in our alternate 1980s Europe. You’ll fight across large, realistic battlefields from German villages to Norwegian terrain, in 40-minute rounds filled with intense infantry combat, armoured warfare and off-map commander abilities - all coming together with team-wide tactical coordination in order to bring the team to victory. 

Every role matters, whether you’re charging in as a rifleman or commanding the battlefield, the action is designed to be intense, immersive, and replayable. 


[previewyoutube="_hL2Ay6gFhY;full"][/previewyoutube]

Authentic Weapons & Gear 
’83 will put the most iconic weapons of the Cold War in your hands, each meticulously designed and animated according to their real-world counterparts from the late 1980s, not just in look and sound, but in behaviour. 

Barrels and suppressors overheat when rapid firing, machineguns are better deployed on a stable surface, and bullets don't magically teleport in between magazines when you reload a half-empty one. 

[img src="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAAAXNSR0IArs4c6QAAAARnQU1BAACxjwv8YQUAAAAJcEhZcwAADsMAAA7DAcdvqGQAAAANSURBVBhXY2BgYGAAAAAFAAGKM+MAAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"]In addition, your soldier's uniform & gear is also meticulously recreated to be accurate to the time period and what unit he is a part of. 


Accessible Realism 
We aim to make everything as realistic as possible, until the point where it stops being fun and becomes tedious instead, then we ratchet it back one notch. 

‘83 is designed to respect your time with action-packed 30-40 minute matches, meaningful roles, and maps that encourage tactical play without turning into a never-ending slog. 

[img src="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAAAXNSR0IArs4c6QAAAARnQU1BAACxjwv8YQUAAAAJcEhZcwAADsMAAA7DAcdvqGQAAAANSURBVBhXY2BgYGAAAAAFAAGKM+MAAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"] 
A Veteran Team 
Many members of the studio were instrumental in shaping Red Orchestra 2 and Rising Storm, so we know tactical shooters, and we’re using that experience to build something new, a true spiritual successor to these much-loved franchises.  

[img src="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAAAXNSR0IArs4c6QAAAARnQU1BAACxjwv8YQUAAAAJcEhZcwAADsMAAA7DAcdvqGQAAAANSURBVBhXY2BgYGAAAAAFAAGKM+MAAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"] 
Built in Unreal Engine 5 
We’re building ‘83 from the ground up in Unreal Engine 5. That gives us powerful tools like Nanite and Lumen to push visual fidelity and realism further than we ever could in previous projects. 

Of course, UE5 is still evolving, and it’s not without its challenges, but we’re pushing hard to get the most out of the engine. You can hear more about how we’re tackling these challenges in our recent interview with MoiDawg. 


[previewyoutube="uXw2UwgYoFg;full"][/previewyoutube]

Early Access Is Coming 
We’ll be launching into Early Access later this year with a focused set of maps and features, and then expanding based on our community’s feedback. Your invaluable input is going to help shape this game throughout Early Access. 

Join our Discord community to stay up-to-date with the latest about ‘83 and get a direct line with the development team themselves! 



 https://discord.gg/JhpgysJuex 


What’s Next? 
In the next dev diary, we’ll be taking a closer look at the two primary factions at the heart of ’83; the United States and the Soviet Union. 

We’ll break down the setting of the conflict, introduce each faction’s tactical identity, and dive into their starting arsenals, from rifles and sidearms to heavy weapons and support gear. You’ll get a sense of how we’re shaping their roles on the battlefield. 

For now, thanks for being here. If you’re into tactical FPS games with weight, atmosphere, and intensity, this one’s for you. 

— Blue Dot Games

notes.title: ‘83 Development Update - Growing the Team
notes.content:
Soldiers!

We would like to say a massive thank you to everyone for your support and feedback since we released our re-announcement trailer, the enthusiasm for ‘83 and what we are building has been brilliant and we’re very excited to share more with you on the road to launch. 

Since the announcement, the ‘83 team has been growing rapidly across development, community, cinematics and marketing, and we plan to share development progress here showcasing updates across different maps, weapons, gameplay mechanics and what to expect when it comes to ‘accessible realism’ in ‘83. 

Development update - April 2025

Our level design team has officially begun crafting brand new environments, expanding the future battlegrounds you'll explore. While we can't reveal specifics just yet, the process of bringing these new locations from concept to reality is well underway and incredibly exciting for us.
 
Simultaneously, we've been dedicating significant effort to refining the core experience. This includes ongoing network optimization work aimed at ensuring smooth, stable online gameplay. Our animation department has also been busy, focusing on enhancing the feel and responsiveness of weapon handling to make those in-game moments even more immersive.
 
Underpinning all of this is our continued work with Unreal Engine 5. We're constantly striving to harness the power of UE5 to deliver the best possible visual fidelity and performance for '83.
It's been a productive period, and the positive energy in the studio is palpable.

Weapons showcase 

The team has also been busy working on a range of different weapons that players can expect to get their hands on when we launch in Early Access this year including the RPG-7, AKS-74U and AK-74, we’re pleased to share some screenshots of these below (with much more to come in future trailers)

notes.title: '83 Development Update – January 2025
notes.content:
Dear ‘83 Community!

We’re excited to bring you our first development update of the new year.

Thanks to the feedback from the 8 playtests we’ve held so far, we’ve been able to make significant strides in server performance. Our code team "assaulted" these challenges head-on, and we’re now able to support sufficient player counts to start showing the fun aspects of the game to testers!

Overall, these tests have been invaluable in helping us debug several critical issues, and it's been great to see players not just fill, and stress test the servers, but also enjoy the game as it’s meant to be played with 75 players running! 

Production Goals for January and February
Looking ahead, we’re now turning our focus towards weapons and animations. This is no small task, as we've essentially had to recreate the animation framework from the ground up. 

Without being too specific (to manage expectations), we also want to give you a look at our overarching production plan for the next two months. Here’s what the team is focused on delivering:

January:

 Rollout of an all-new animation framework
 Significant progress on weapons systems

February:

 Continued optimization along with key additions and tweaks to core gameplay systems
 Full Integration of Unreal Engine 5 features like Nanite and Virtual Shadow Maps for visually stunning environments with a manageable GPU load
 Deeper exploration of UE5's IRIS networking architecture, which we aim to leverage for smoother, large-scale multiplayer performance

The Path to Our Vertical Slice
By the end of February, we’re aiming to achieve a critical milestone of the ’83 project: the vertical slice build. We’ve had many of you asking what specifically that means – roughly, this is the gist of it:

[olist]
 "Show the Fun in ‘83": A showcase of one example map where core gameplay loop of ’83 shows its main fun element
 Core Gameplay Systems: Demonstrate most of the core systems that define the ‘83 experience
 Graphics Optimizations: We’re aiming to implement Nanites and Virtual Shadow Maps to deliver the best possible visuals along with scalable performance
 Server Stability: Further optimize the game to support for 80-player servers without server CPU or network hiccups
 Gather more HW spec data: Collection of data to define accurate minimum and recommended system requirements.
[/olist]
Closing Thoughts
The year is off to a great start, and we’d like to thank all of you for your continued support and enthusiasm. Your feedback and participation in playtests have helped shape the game into what it is today, and we can’t wait to show you what we’ve been building as we move closer to our vertical slice goals.

We’re also excited to report that we’re putting additional focus on the marketing side of things – and we want to deliver a proper update to our Steam page in January, including new screenshots and a trailer. 

Stay tuned for more updates!

The 83 Development Team

notes.title: '83 Development Update: now Improving Net Code to Allow Playtesting!
notes.content:
Dear community,

We're excited to update you on '83's development journey. Our team is working hard on our current primary objective: to get a stable build ready for closed community playtests, with the main hurdle so far being sub-par network performance. 

Fortunately, running the game on a powerful bare metal Windows server (as opposed to the standard, more cost effective cloud-powered virtual machine we aim to use) offers acceptable performance and enables us to begin some level of testing – as we proved in a short, closed test earlier this weekend.

Our progress in net code optimization is now driven by a talented duo of experienced programmers, which marks a significant improvement from a few months ago when we solely relied on volunteers. The development ultimately moved from a slow crawl to a steady jog and we are continuously gaining momentum!

Thank you for your ongoing support and patience as we continue to bring '83 to life. Your feedback is invaluable, so stay tuned for more updates!

o7

notes.title: '83 is Officially Back in Development at Blue Dot Games studio!
notes.content:
Dear '83 Steam Community! 

At Blue Dot Games, we're excited to let you know that after a long period of downtime, we're officially resuming development of the '83 project!

Some of you may have noticed our earlier announcements (we acquired the rights for '83 back in 2023, and had a short segment at the #PCGamingShow this summer) but we did not have the funds to support an actual professional team of paid developers.

That changes today!

After a long series of meetings and negotiations with various investors and publishers, the funding came from the most unexpected place of the games industry: our Discord server! ːsteamthumbsupː
